title: F. Alice's Adventures in Addition
statement:
Note that the memory limit is unusual.

The Cheshire Cat has a riddle for Alice: given n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n and a target m, is there a way to insert + and × into the circles of the expression a_1 circ a_2 circ ⋯ circ a_n = m to make it true? We follow the usual order of operations: × is done before +.

Although Alice is excellent at chess, she is not good at math. Please help her so she can find a way out of Wonderland!

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n, m (1≤ n≤ 2·10^5; 1≤ m≤ 10^4) — the number of integers and the target, respectively.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (0≤ a_i≤ 10^4) — the elements of the array a.

The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

For each test case, output "YES" without quotes if it is possible to get the target by inserting + or × and "NO" otherwise.

You can output each letter in any case (for example, the strings "yEs", "yes", "Yes", and "YES" will be recognized as a positive answer).

Possible solutions for the first four test cases are shown below. beginalign* 2 × 1 + 1 × 1 × 2 &= 4 2 × 1 + 1 + 1 × 2 &= 5 2 × 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 &= 6 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 &= 7 endalign* It is impossible to get a result of 8 in the fifth test case.

Input:
```
65 42 1 1 1 25 52 1 1 1 25 62 1 1 1 25 72 1 1 1 25 82 1 1 1 25 62 0 2 2 3
```

Output:
```
YES
YES
YES
YES
NO
YES
```
